notes: Secret Morse (one-to-one chats and the Morse screen): your message becomes a code made from your and your contact's private keys, with a new code for every message. Only your two phones can decode it; the recipient sees the decoded text automatically, and anyone who hears or sees the Morse only gets the code. Plain text is never stored. It is modern encryption, not a one-time pad (the one-time pad is still available).

Contacts added only by their key can now be reached: Vexunori publishes the relays where you receive messages (NIP-17 inbox relay list; can be turned off in Settings → Relays) and looks up your contacts' lists, also via the purplepag.es directory.
Privacy Center shows whether a VPN is on (Android), with a guide to using Proton VPN Free alongside Vexunori. New Android permission: ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE (connection type only, no prompt).
Settings → Tor explains what to do when Tor is blocked (Orbot with bridges). Built-in bridges are not included because the bridge library contains GPL code.
Disguise: without a passphrase or PIN you can now get back in with your secret key if you forget the code.
Still experimental and untested on many real phones — please report bugs on GitHub.
